newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Georgia has no claim on Black Sea Fleet -Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Georgia has no claim on Black Sea Fleet -Kremlin.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Georgia has no claim to any ships of the long-disputed Black Sea Fleet, the Kremlin said on Friday.
"Georgia has no right to demand a part in the division of the Black Sea Fleet," said Sergei Yastrzhembsky, spokesman for Russian President Boris Yeltsin, as quoted by Interfax news agency.

The prime ministers of Russia and Ukraine said they had settled a protracted dispute over a shareout of the former Soviet fleet on Wednesday by leasing naval facilities at its headquarters in Sevastopol, Crimea to Russia for 20 years.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin was due to start a two-day visit to the Ukrainian capital Kiev on Friday afternoon. He was expected to sign a friendship and cooperation treaty with Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma, long delayed by rows over who gets what of the now rusting navy.

Earlier, Archil Gegeshidze, Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze's national security adviser, told Interfax the tiny mountainous state would continue to demand what it sees as its share of the fleet.
"The matter is for Georgia to receive what to a certain degree is its property," Gegeshidze said, cited by the agency.
On Wednesday, Shevardnadze said Soviet-built ships based in the Georgian port of Poti had been spirited away in 1992 "without the agreement and without consultation with the Georgian government".
But Yastrzhembsky cited a decision made by leaders of the Commonwealth of Independent States in April 1992 which restricted the division of the fleet to Russia and Ukraine.
He added that Georgia in 1991 "nationalised" Poti and that the equipment and property left at the port were equivalent in value to the ships that had been based there.
"In this sense, from the legal and economic points of view, Georgia's claims have no foundation," Yastrzhembksy said.
Itar-Tass also quoted Shevardnadze as saying he had sent two written messages to Yeltsin recently, calling his attention to Georgia's desire for part of the fleet, but had received no reply.
Georgia has about 350 km (250 miles) of coastline on the Black Sea. Half of that is controlled by the secessionist leadership of its Abkhazia province.
